title: On Bothering the doctor after midnight
subtitle: 人际沟通 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 人际沟通（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·人际沟通与交流）
meta: 主题语境：人际沟通（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·人际沟通与交流）　|　核心词汇：bother　|　正文 329 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 bother 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1984 the cook ① bothered the doctor after midnight before dawn, and every guest in the canteen said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three days on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the cook ② bothers the doctor after midnight in public without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ bother the doctor after midnight at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ bothered the doctor after midnight before — a line in the menu for September 1978 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Bothering the doctor after midnight before dawn, the cook said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the bowl at the far table, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ bother about such small matters in public, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Bother about such small matters at once and never mention it again.

By 1991 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the menu, and a new guest from the next canteen ⑧ bothers about such small matters before dawn every day without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the table, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ bothered the doctor after midnight again when nobody else would.

⑩ To bother the doctor after midnight, my mother said in 1996, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the canteen remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the canteen forgets, somebody bothers the doctor after midnight in public again and somebody must bother the doctor after midnight before dawn all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 打扰（一般过去式 bothered the doctor after midnight：1984 年厨子头一回这样做，天没亮就）
B. v. 打扰（一般现在 bothers the doctor after midnight：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 打扰（不定式 to bother the doctor after midnight：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 打扰（过去完成时 had bothered the doctor after midnight：1978 年九月的菜单上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 打扰（动名词 bothering the doctor after midnight 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 费神（bother about such small matters：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去费神为这点小事费神）
G. v. 费神（bother about such small matters：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 打扰（后段两处：新来的客人照例 bothers about such small matters，而母亲又一次 bothered the doctor after midnight）

items.q: to bother the doctor after midnight
bothered the doctor after midnight before

answers.why: bother 意为“打扰”，1984 年厨子天没亮就打扰半夜过后去惊动医生，那是食堂里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 bothered。
bother 意为“打扰”，自那以后厨子当着众人面把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 bothers。
bother 意为“打扰”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯打扰半夜过后去惊动医生”，此处为不定式 to bother the doctor after midnight。
bother 意为“打扰”，菜单里 九月 那行字说明早在 1991 年之前就有人打扰过，故用过去完成时 had bothered。
bother 意为“打扰”，厨子说“打扰半夜过后去惊动医生这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 bothering the doctor after midnight 作主语。
bother 意为“费神”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去费神为这点小事费神”，should ever 之后用原形 bother about such small matters。
bother 意为“费神”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻费神为这点小事费神（bother about such small matters at once），以后再也不要提起。
bother 意为“打扰”，新来的客人每个日子都照例费神为这点小事费神，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 bothers。
bother 意为“打扰”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次天没亮就打扰半夜过后去惊动医生，用一般过去式 bothered 叙述。
bother 意为“打扰”，结尾那句是母亲 1996 年的话：要打扰半夜过后去惊动医生，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和食堂记住的那一件。

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 bother 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1984 the cook bothered the doctor after midnight before dawn, and nobody in the canteen forgot it.
Even now the cook bothers the doctor after midnight in public whenever the canteen asks.
Bothering the doctor after midnight before dawn, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever bother about such small matters in public, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new guest from the next canteen bothers about such small matters before dawn every day, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother bothered the doctor after midnight again, and the canteen remembered that half.
